A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DDPN research. Their main texts and complete appendices are readable, with figures, tables, and equations available for reliable comparison despite substantial revision and reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original simulations, experiments on five real-world datasets, OOD analyses, and appendix results covering beta sensitivity and multiclass alternatives.

after.justification: v3 reports original simulations, experiments on four real-world datasets, OOD detection results, and appendix analyses of moment approximations, initialization sensitivity, and predictive sharpness.

M1.justification: The Double Poisson predictive head, approximate NLL objective, stop-gradient beta weighting, and uniform-mixture ensemble procedure are retained. Renaming inverse dispersion from phi to gamma, explicitly writing head biases, and explaining the omitted normalizer do not establish a change to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 replaces Bikes and Collision with hospital Length of Stay, substantially changing tabular task coverage. COCO-People, Inventory, Amazon Reviews, and the Reviews-versus-Bible OOD scenario remain. The synthetic recovery experiments add Poisson-generated data alongside the existing negative-binomial scenario.

E2.justification: v3 adds beta=1 Gaussian comparisons and ensembles of Faithful, Natural, and beta-Gaussian models, substantially expanding the ensemble comparator set. It also adds GLM ensembles in Table 5 and removes the multiclass NN comparisons on Inventory and Reviews. Faithful, Natural, and beta=0.5 Gaussian match v2's Stirn, Immer, and Seitzer baselines rather than representing new methods.

E3.justification: Calibration evaluation changes from continuity-corrected NLL to CRPS, and checkpoint selection changes from validation MAE to validation loss. COCO learning rate and weight decay change; Reviews training changes from updating the backbone to freezing all but its final transformer block. OOD evaluation becomes variance-threshold classification with a 20% ID holdout and AUROC, AUPR, and FPR80. These are substantive reported protocol revisions.

E4.justification: v3 adds empirical moment-approximation error maps, initialization sensitivity with and without beta weighting, median-precision analysis, and Length of Stay CDF case studies. It revises the simulation to analyze ensemble uncertainty components and expands qualitative model comparisons. The COCO beta grid search and multiclass pathology analysis disappear, while the existing three-beta convergence illustration is retained.

E5.justification: The main regression experiments retain five trained models and mean/standard-deviation reporting. OOD permutation tests using 1,500 permutations and associated p-values are replaced by means and standard deviations across ten holdout-resampling evaluations; these are not ten training runs. The GLM appendix additionally describes its reported spread as standard error, inconsistently with the main text's standard-deviation convention.

E6.justification: Results are extensively replaced and added. For example, beta=1 DDPN ensemble MAE changes from 1.701 to 0.959 on COCO-People and from 0.281 to 0.344 on Reviews (v2 Table 3; v3 Table 2). Training and selection changed, so these are not same-setting gains or losses. v3 adds CRPS, sharpness, Length of Stay, and OOD classification results while removing the earlier NLL, entropy-gap, and multiclass results.

T1.justification: v3 introduces formal definitions of unrestricted variance, full heteroscedasticity, and learnable loss attenuation, with propositions and proofs in Sections 2–3 and Appendix C. Appendix A.3 adds moment-deviation functions and their derivation, explicitly qualifying DDPN's heteroscedasticity through approximate moments. These substantially extend v2's loss derivation and standard mixture formulas.

C1.justification: v3 adds formalization and proof of learnable loss attenuation as a central contribution and emphasizes improved epistemic uncertainty through fully heteroscedastic ensembles. Its abstract and conclusion strengthen v2's claim of matching or exceeding Gaussian methods to outperforming the evaluated baselines in accuracy, calibration, and OOD detection. The conclusion also newly claims uncorrupted epistemic estimates.

C2.justification: v2 presents beta primarily as an accuracy-versus-calibration/OOD tradeoff; v3 argues it can improve both MAE and CRPS and positively interprets beta ensembles' OOD behavior under the revised evaluation. New explanations connect aleatoric misspecification to epistemic error and attribute performance to loss attenuation and discrete inductive bias. Appendix A.3 specifies approximation deterioration at small means with large target variance.

D1.justification: v3 supplies a Length of Stay training recipe, explicit dataset sizes, revised hardware and trainable-layer details, and additional reproducibility instructions. The advertised code location changes from an anonymous repository to a named GitHub repository, with configuration-file pointers and instructions for obtaining prepared splits. Some information is lost: v3 no longer states the COCO epoch budget or Inventory split proportions explicitly.

R1.justification: v3 substantially develops positioning around deep ensembles, uncertainty entanglement, and the claimed first formalization of learnable loss attenuation. It adds relevant literature including Mucsanyi et al., Osband et al., scoring-rule work, and OOD detection references. Its treatment of prior Double Poisson regression now acknowledges joint GLMs with separate dispersion covariates, refining v2's blanket description of follow-up models as using constant dispersion.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Related-work subsections are reordered, real-world experiments are consolidated, misspecification recovery moves into the main text, and the appendices are reorganized around derivations, experimental details, proofs, and case studies. The title changes from Flexible to Fully Heteroscedastic.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one to two columns, and major displays are redesigned. The introductory simulation gains separate aleatoric and epistemic panels; the architecture schematic depicts ensembles. Benchmark reporting is consolidated, new OOD and sharpness tables appear, and appendix case studies are extensively rearranged. The old beta schematic, grid-search plot, and entropy KDE displays disappear; the Inventory point-cloud illustration is retained.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens validation of the paper's central uncertainty claims through direct OOD detection metrics, broader ensemble comparisons, and investigation of the moment-approximation gap explicitly acknowledged in v2. Initialization and sharpness analyses add useful diagnostic evidence. Removing Bikes, Collision, and multiclass comparisons reduces breadth, and OOD evidence still covers only one task, but the more direct evaluation and clearer treatment of assumptions outweigh these losses.
